title: Event-store migrations run through a release entry point, not mix
rationale: Local development and the integration tests both shell out to 'mix ecto.migrate', which hides this gap: the migration path works everywhere except the artifact that actually ships. Any future migration must be reachable from the release, not just from the mix project.

description: ForemanServer.Http.Endpoint hard-coded its Bandit bind address to {127,0,0,1} with no override, so a container's published port and a k8s Service could never reach the API. The failure mode is a silent TIMEOUT rather than an error, which reads like a cluster networking or Service-selector problem — the server logs look completely healthy and /api/v1/health answers fine from inside the container.
resolution: Added FOREMAN_SERVER_HTTP_BIND (ForemanServer.Http.Endpoint.bind_ip/0), which still DEFAULTS TO LOOPBACK and falls back to loopback on an unparseable value; the container image sets 0.0.0.0. The pre-existing validate_remote_access!/1 guard is what makes widening safe: binding beyond loopback without FOREMAN_SERVER_AUTH_TOKEN raises at startup (verified exit 1 in the container, not just in tests). Keep that pairing — a wider default bind without the token guard would expose the orchestrator control plane unauthenticated.

description: The PreToolUse tool-policy hook was installed into a kelos agent pod via Task.spec.preCommands, with its Claude Code settings written to /tmp/foreman/claude-settings.json. The live phase SUCCEEDED, the agent's Bash call ran, and permission_denials was empty — the gate never fired. Claude Code only loads settings from $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/settings.json (default $HOME/.claude); a settings file anywhere else is silently ignored. Every unit test passed because they asserted the file was WRITTEN, not that anything reads that path; a clean-container test and direct endpoint tests also passed. The failure presented as success (green Task, exit 0, agent reporting the command worked) which is exactly the 'looks protected while every tool call goes unchecked' mode the gate exists to prevent.
resolution: Write settings to ${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json, resolved by the POD's shell rather than by Node path helpers (dirname would mangle the shell expansion). Verified by re-dispatching a real phase: the agent's Bash call returned 'PreToolUse:Bash hook error: Foreman tool policy: explorer must use Grep/Glob/Read discovery', permission_denials recorded the call, and the agent reported the command never executed. LESSON: for any hook/config injected into a pod, verify the CONSUMER reads that path — a write-side assertion proves nothing. Only a live dispatch caught this.

title: Patch transport stays the default; EBS volume transport declined (AZ-pinned)
rationale: Patch transport (agent uploads a git patch to object storage, Foreman applies it) needs no shared filesystem, no shared AZ, and no shared node, so it has none of these constraints. The AZ pinning is a property of EBS, not of the plan's node-affinity framing — node affinity alone does not solve it. Revisit ONLY with ReadWriteMany storage (EFS), which is AZ-independent and would remove the pinning entirely; EFS was considered and declined for this cluster. Do not build volume transport against EBS.

description: The build-atomic.js asset filter allowed only extensionless/.md/.yaml files, so no .sh ever reached dist/. Pod-side hooks (tool policy, Agent Mail) resolve dist/defaults first and fall back to src/defaults; because package.json also ships src/defaults, the fallback always succeeded locally and the packaging gap was invisible. A loader fallback that works in every local layout hides a packaging bug until it runs somewhere the fallback is absent.
resolution: Added .sh to the build-atomic.js filter and pinned it with a test. When a loader has a src/ fallback, assert the asset resolves from dist/ specifically — not merely that the loader returns some path.
